hook: Two analysts model a channel's followers. One fits a line, the other an exponential function, and both graphs look close to the data. The residuals, the misses each model makes, decide which one to trust for next month.

prereq.q: Over equal steps, outputs go $100, 125, 156.25$. What fits?
What does a calculator regression do?
options: Finds the constants of a chosen model type that fit all the data closest
Finds a model through exactly two points
Chooses the model type for you
prereq.why: You choose the type; the regression chooses the constants.

figure.caption: Residuals (actual minus predicted) of two models of the same data. The linear model's residuals form a U; the exponential model's scatter near 0 with no pattern, so it is the more appropriate model.

chain.cause: For each data point, subtract the prediction from the actual value
chain.effect: the residuals: positive where the model underestimates, negative where it overestimates

chain.cause: Plot the residuals against the input

chain.effect: the model is appropriate; a curve or trend means it misses the shape of the data

ideas: Residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted. Positive: the model underestimates. Negative: it overestimates.
An appropriate model has a residual plot scattered around 0 with no pattern; a U or a trend shows the model has the wrong shape.
Error can also be stated as predicted $-$ actual, or as an absolute error $|\text{predicted} - \text{actual}|$. Compare competing models by their residuals.

misconception.wrong: If a model's residuals are both positive and negative, the model fits well.
misconception.right: Mixed signs are expected; what matters is the pattern. Residuals that go positive, negative, positive in order show a curve the model misses.

summary: Residuals (actual minus predicted) measure how far a model misses each data point. Choose the model whose residuals are small and patternless, and read the sign of the residuals to say where a model underestimates or overestimates.
